headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Goose’s filesystem/MCP access can ingest Dexter outputs and act on them without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can emit files in .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while Goose reads/writes the user filesystem and uses MCP extensions. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where Dexter-produced text can be treated as instructions by Goose. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dexter writes attacker-controlled text into .dexter/scratchpad/ and Goose reads that file as context, injection is possible.
IF Goose is configured to ingest workspace files without provenance filtering, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Dexter and Goose in separate directories.
Disable automatic file ingestion for Goose.
Require manual review of any Dexter-generated text before Goose reads it.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs, while Goose reads the filesystem and also has broad network egress via configured providers and MCP servers. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from Dexter into Goose and then out through Goose’s networked tools. The blast radius includes exfiltration of financial data.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace, Goose can read Dexter artifacts containing financial data.
IF Goose forwards those artifacts to configured model providers or MCP servers, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Remove sensitive files from any shared cwd.
Disable Goose network access for sessions handling Dexter outputs.
Restrict Dexter outputs to redacted summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances via filesystem-shared state; Dexter also supports multiple instances and writes scratchpad files. In a shared repo or cwd, both can mutate overlapping state without documented locking, so concurrent writes and git conflicts are likely in default use.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same git checkout, concurrent edits can collide.
IF Dexter writes scratchpad artifacts while Goose edits tracked files, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate git branches per agent.
Use separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit Goose changes before Dexter runs.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking and merge coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can autonomously execute workflows and call external APIs, while Goose can use MCP tools and shell execution. If Goose treats Dexter outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or code changes. The pair does not document a verification barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Goose consumes Dexter-generated recommendations without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF Dexter outputs are used as inputs to Goose tool calls, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Require human review before Goose acts on Dexter output.
Add a verification checklist for any Dexter-derived instruction.
Limit Goose to read-only mode for Dexter-produced artifacts.
Log and diff all downstream actions.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Goose handles files in the user filesystem and can send content to configured model providers. If regulated financial data is placed in Goose’s workspace, retention and residency obligations may diverge from Dexter’s handling. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in Goose-accessible files, compliance obligations apply.
IF Goose forwards those files to third-party model providers, residency or retention mismatches may occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose workspaces.
Redact financial identifiers before sharing artifacts.
Review provider retention settings before each session.
Use local-only models for sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy per agent.
